anomalies.observed: On the Serial sheet, SC16IS752 devices U13 and U14 have pin 9 (I2C/SPI) tied directly to GND. The same devices are wired for SPI operation: pin 10 (A0/CS) carries CS1/CS2, pin 11 (A1/SI) carries SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 (SD/SO) carries SERIAL_CIPO, and pin 13 (SCL/SCLK) carries SERIAL_CLK.
anomalies.expected: For SC16IS752, pin 9 is the I2C/SPI mode-select pin; logic high selects SPI mode and logic low selects I2C mode. Because the surrounding nets are clearly SPI signals (CS, COPI, CIPO, SCLK), pin 9 should be pulled high to the device VDD rail (SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V), not tied to GND.

evidence.quote: U13 SC16IS752 ... pin 9 I2C/SPI connected to GND; pin 10 A0/CS = CS1; pin 11 A1/SI = SERIAL_COPI; pin 12 SD = SERIAL_CIPO; pin 13 SCL/SCLK = SERIAL_CLK
U14 SC16IS752 ... pin 9 I2C/SPI connected to GND; pin 10 A0/CS = CS2; pin 11 A1/SI = SERIAL_COPI; pin 12 SD = SERIAL_CIPO; pin 13 SCL/SCLK = SERIAL_CLK

anomalies.impact: Both UART-to-SPI/I2C bridges are forced into I2C mode while the board is wired for SPI. The serial expansion paths driven by SERIAL_COPI/CIPO/CLK and CS1/CS2 will not communicate correctly, making the associated serial interfaces nonfunctional.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears largely consistent with the specification, but the SC16IS752 mode-select pins are tied to ground while the rest of the circuit uses SPI signals, which is a likely design error.
